chapters.subject: Mathematics
chapters.title: Rational Numbers & Fractions
chapters.introduction: Rational numbers form the bedrock of algebra and real-world arithmetic. In this chapter, we explore fractional representations, equivalent rational numbers, addition and subtraction using least common denominators (LCM), reciprocal multiplication, and word problem modeling.
learningObjectives: Understand the formal definition of rational numbers in p/q form (q ≠ 0)
Master fraction reduction to lowest terms using GCD/HCF
Add and subtract fractions with like and unlike denominators using LCM
Multiply rational numbers and understand the concept of reciprocal/multiplicative inverse
Solve multi-step real-world problems involving fractional parts

concepts.title: Concept of Rational Numbers & Equivalence
concepts.description: Numbers expressible as p/q where p and q are integers and q is non-zero.
concepts.learningOutcome: Represent rational numbers on number lines and determine equivalence.

concepts.title: Fraction Simplification & Lowest Terms
concepts.description: Dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor (GCD).
concepts.learningOutcome: Reduce any fraction to its simplest irreducible form.

concepts.title: Addition & Subtraction of Unlike Fractions (LCM Method)
concepts.description: Aligning denominators using the Least Common Multiple (LCM) before combining numerators.
concepts.learningOutcome: Accurately compute sums and differences of unlike rational numbers without adding denominators.

concepts.title: Multiplication & Reciprocals of Rational Numbers
concepts.description: Direct numerator-by-numerator and denominator-by-denominator multiplication, and multiplicative inverses.
concepts.learningOutcome: Divide rational numbers by multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor.

chapters.subject: Mathematics
chapters.title: Linear Equations in One Variable
chapters.introduction: Linear equations are mathematical statements where an expression with a degree-1 variable equals another expression or constant. Mastering balancing methods and the transposition rule unlocks problem solving in science, geometry, and finance.
learningObjectives: Distinguish algebraic expressions from algebraic equations
Solve linear equations using the balancing property of equality
Apply the transposition method with strict sign-reversal discipline
Solve linear equations having variables on both sides
Formulate and solve real-world word problems from word statements

concepts.title: Equations vs Expressions & Degree of a Variable
concepts.description: Understanding equations as balances containing an equals sign (=) with highest power 1.
concepts.learningOutcome: Identify linear equations and verify solutions by substitution.

concepts.title: Transposition Method & Sign Reversal
concepts.description: Moving terms across the equals sign by changing positive to negative and multiplication to division.
concepts.learningOutcome: Isolate variables without making sign errors during transposition.

concepts.title: Equations with Variables on Both Sides
concepts.description: Grouping variable terms on the LHS and constant terms on the RHS.
concepts.learningOutcome: Solve multi-term equations involving brackets and fractions.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Force and Pressure
chapters.introduction: Force is an interaction that, when unopposed, changes the motion of an object. Pressure is the magnitude of force exerted per unit area.
learningObjectives: Understand push or pull as force
Differentiate contact and non-contact forces
Calculate pressure using Pressure = Force / Area
Examine atmospheric and fluid pressure

concepts.title: Nature of Force: Contact vs Non-Contact
concepts.description: Muscular and friction forces vs gravitational, electrostatic, and magnetic forces.
concepts.learningOutcome: Classify everyday interactions into contact and field forces.

concepts.title: Pressure and Surface Area Relationship
concepts.description: For a given force, a smaller surface area results in greater pressure.
concepts.learningOutcome: Apply P = F/A to explain sharp knives, wide camel feet, and foundation structures.

chapters.subject: Physical Science
chapters.title: Metals and Non-Metals
chapters.introduction: SCERT Telangana Physical Science curriculum investigates the physical properties (malleability, ductility, sonority, conductivity) and chemical reactions of metallic and non-metallic elements.
learningObjectives: Analyze malleability, ductility, sonority and conductivity of elements
Observe reactions of metals with oxygen, water and acids
Compare acidic vs basic nature of metallic and non-metallic oxides

concepts.title: Physical Properties of Metals and Non-Metals
concepts.description: Distinguishing elements based on luster, conductivity, ductility, and malleability.
concepts.learningOutcome: Identify metals and non-metals experimentally.

concepts.title: Chemical Reactions with Oxygen & Oxides Nature
concepts.description: Metal oxides are basic (turn red litmus blue); non-metal oxides are acidic (turn blue litmus red).
concepts.learningOutcome: Predict litmus indicator color changes for metallic vs non-metallic oxides.

chapters.subject: Biological Science
chapters.title: Cell: The Basic Unit of Life
chapters.introduction: SCERT Telangana Biological Science curriculum introduces the discovery of cells by Robert Hooke, microscopic observation of onion peel and cheek cells, and the structural differences between plant and animal cells.
learningObjectives: Understand historical discovery of the cell
Identify cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, and cell wall
Compare plant cells with animal cells

concepts.title: Cell Organelles: Nucleus, Membrane & Cell Wall
concepts.description: The distinct functions of boundary layers and the control center of the cell.
concepts.learningOutcome: Distinguish animal cells from plant cells by the presence of cell walls and plastids.

chapters.subject: Mathematics
chapters.title: Linear Equations in One Variable (SCERT)
chapters.introduction: SCERT Telangana Class VIII Mathematics syllabus focusing on solving equations using transposition and balancing with applications to age, currency, and geometry problems.
learningObjectives: Solve simple linear equations in one variable
Apply the transposition method with strict sign preservation
Formulate mathematical equations for practical real-life scenarios

concepts.title: Transposition and Balancing Equations
concepts.description: Solving linear equations with variables on one or both sides.
concepts.learningOutcome: Accurately transpose terms without sign inversions.

chapters.subject: Computer Studies
chapters.title: Algorithms and Flowcharts
chapters.introduction: CISCE Upper Primary framework for Computer Studies: computational thinking, algorithmic steps, standard flowchart symbols, and decision logic.
learningObjectives: Define algorithm as finite sequential instructions
Identify flowchart symbols: oval (terminator), parallelogram (I/O), rectangle (process), diamond (decision)
Trace execution and identify logic errors

concepts.title: Flowchart Symbols & Decision Making
concepts.description: Mapping conditional branching (if-then-else) using diamond decision symbols.
concepts.learningOutcome: Construct correct flowcharts for conditional problems.

chapters.subject: Mathematics
chapters.title: Fractions & Representation
chapters.introduction: Foundational introduction to parts of a whole, proper/improper fractions, and number line representation.
learningObjectives: Understand fraction as a part of a whole or collection
Plot fractions on a number line
Convert between improper and mixed fractions

concepts.title: Fractions as Parts of a Whole
concepts.description: Numerator represents selected parts; denominator represents total equal parts.
concepts.learningOutcome: Identify and write fractions from shaded diagrams.

chapters.subject: General Science
chapters.title: Knowing About Plants
chapters.introduction: Telangana SCERT Class 6 General Science exploring roots (taproot vs fibrous), stem transport, and leaf venation.
learningObjectives: Differentiate tap root and fibrous root systems
Relate leaf venation with root types
Understand basic leaf functions including photosynthesis and transpiration

concepts.title: Roots and Leaf Venation Correlation
concepts.description: Reticulate venation correlates with taproot; parallel venation correlates with fibrous roots.
concepts.learningOutcome: Predict root structure by examining leaf venation.

chapters.subject: Mathematics
chapters.title: Factors, Multiples & Prime Numbers
chapters.introduction: CISCE Upper Primary Mathematics: properties of numbers, prime factorization, and HCF/LCM.
learningObjectives: Determine factors and multiples of natural numbers
Perform prime factorization using factor trees or division
Calculate HCF and LCM of numbers

concepts.title: Prime Factorization & LCM Calculation
concepts.description: Expressing composite numbers as products of primes to determine LCM.
concepts.learningOutcome: Find LCM accurately using continuous prime division.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Nutrition in Plants
chapters.introduction: NCERT Class 7 Science: Modes of nutrition, autotrophic vs heterotrophic, photosynthesis mechanism, and saprotrophs.
learningObjectives: Explain photosynthesis equation: Carbon dioxide + Water -> Carbohydrate + Oxygen
Identify role of chlorophyll, stomata and sunlight
Distinguish parasitic, insectivorous, and saprotrophic modes

concepts.title: Autotrophic Nutrition & Photosynthesis
concepts.description: Plants synthesize glucose using sunlight, chlorophyll, CO2, and water.
concepts.learningOutcome: Describe the essential inputs and products of photosynthesis.

chapters.subject: General Science
chapters.title: Motion and Time
chapters.introduction: SCERT Telangana Class 7 General Science: Measurement of time, uniform and non-uniform motion, calculating speed.
learningObjectives: Define speed as distance divided by time
Convert between km/h and m/s
Interpret distance-time graphs

concepts.title: Speed Calculation & Uniform Motion
concepts.description: Formula Speed = Distance / Time and standard SI units.
concepts.learningOutcome: Calculate unknown parameters using Speed = Distance / Time.

chapters.subject: Chemistry
chapters.title: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures
chapters.introduction: CISCE Class 7 Chemistry curriculum: Classification of matter, chemical formulas, and separation techniques.
learningObjectives: Differentiate pure substances from mixtures
Recognize chemical symbols and formulas
Select separation methods like filtration, evaporation, distillation

concepts.title: Compounds vs Mixtures Characteristics
concepts.description: Compounds have fixed ratios and chemical bonds; mixtures have variable composition.
concepts.learningOutcome: Distinguish compounds from mixtures by physical separation feasibility.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Matter in Our Surroundings
chapters.introduction: NCERT Class 9 Science: Particle nature of matter, characteristics of particles, states of matter, latent heat, and evaporation.
learningObjectives: Examine particle spaces, attraction, and kinetic energy
Explain state transitions using temperature and pressure
Understand latent heat of fusion and vaporization

concepts.title: States of Matter & Latent Heat
concepts.description: Intermolecular forces vs thermal energy during phase changes.
concepts.learningOutcome: Explain why temperature stays constant during melting and boiling.

chapters.subject: Physical Science
chapters.title: Laws of Motion
chapters.introduction: SCERT Telangana Class 9 Physical Science: Aristotle vs Galileo views, Newton’s three laws of motion, inertia, momentum, and impulse.
learningObjectives: Define inertia and apply Newton’s first law
Derive F = ma from rate of change of momentum
Analyze action-reaction pairs in Newton’s third law

concepts.title: Newton’s Second Law & Momentum Calculation
concepts.description: Force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma) and conservation of momentum.
concepts.learningOutcome: Calculate net force, acceleration, and change in momentum.

chapters.subject: Physics
chapters.title: Motion in One Dimension
chapters.introduction: ICSE Class 9 Physics: Scalars and vectors, speed, velocity, acceleration, equations of uniformly accelerated motion.
learningObjectives: Differentiate scalar and vector quantities
Apply equations: v = u + at, s = ut + 0.5at², v² = u² + 2as
Interpret velocity-time graphs for acceleration and distance

concepts.title: Kinematic Equations for Uniform Acceleration
concepts.description: Solving numerical problems using the three kinematic equations.
concepts.learningOutcome: Select and calculate the appropriate equation of motion given initial conditions.

chapters.subject: Mathematics
chapters.title: Real Numbers & Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
chapters.introduction: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, proving irrationality of √2, √3, √5, and decimal expansions of rational numbers.
learningObjectives: State and apply the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
Compute HCF and LCM of polynomials and composite numbers
Prove irrationality of numbers using proof by contradiction

concepts.title: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic & Proof of Irrationality
concepts.description: Every composite number can be uniquely expressed as a product of primes.
concepts.learningOutcome: Construct rigorous proofs of irrationality using contradiction.

chapters.subject: Physical Science
chapters.title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
chapters.introduction: SCERT Telangana Class 10 Physical Science: Chemical equations, balancing chemical equations, types of reactions, oxidation and reduction, corrosion and rancidity.
learningObjectives: Write balanced chemical equations with state symbols
Categorize combination, decomposition, displacement, and double displacement
Identify oxidizing and reducing agents in redox reactions

concepts.title: Balancing Chemical Equations & Redox Reactions
concepts.description: Conservation of mass in chemical reactions and electron transfer/oxygen-hydrogen tracking.
concepts.learningOutcome: Balance multi-reactant equations and identify oxidation states.

chapters.subject: Physics
chapters.title: Force, Work, Power and Energy
chapters.introduction: ICSE Class 10 Physics: Turning effect of a force (moment of force), equilibrium, center of gravity, work, power, kinetic and potential energy conservation.
learningObjectives: Calculate moment of force: Force × Perpendicular distance
State the principle of moments for a body in rotational equilibrium
Relate kinetic energy (0.5mv²) and potential energy (mgh) in free fall

concepts.title: Moment of Force & Principle of Moments
concepts.description: Clockwise moment equals counter-clockwise moment in rotational balance.
concepts.learningOutcome: Solve lever and meter-rule balancing problems using the principle of moments.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
chapters.introduction: A chemical reaction is a process where the reactant substances undergo chemical transformation to form new products with entirely different properties. In this chapter, we master writing balanced chemical equations obeying mass conservation, identify types of reactions (combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, redox), and investigate everyday oxidation phenomena like corrosion and rancidity.
learningObjectives: Write word equations and translate them into balanced skeletal chemical equations
Balance chemical equations using the hit-and-trial method with state symbols (s, l, g, aq)
Classify reactions into exothermic, endothermic, combination, and decomposition types
Distinguish oxidation (loss of electrons / addition of oxygen) from reduction (gain of electrons / addition of hydrogen)
Explain practical prevention techniques for metal corrosion and food rancidity

concepts.title: Balancing Chemical Equations & Law of Conservation of Mass
concepts.description: Ensuring equal counts of each atomic species on both reactant and product sides.
concepts.learningOutcome: Balance multi-element reactions with correct state symbols.

concepts.title: Types of Reactions & Redox Phenomena
concepts.description: Combination, decomposition, displacement, and simultaneous oxidation-reduction processes.
concepts.learningOutcome: Identify oxidizing and reducing agents in chemical redox equations.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Life Processes (Nutrition, Respiration, Circulation & Excretion)
chapters.introduction: All living organisms maintain life through essential biological processes: nutrition (autotrophic & heterotrophic), cellular respiration (aerobic vs anaerobic), internal transport (human circulatory system, xylem/phloem in plants), and metabolic excretion via nephrons.
learningObjectives: Understand the biochemical mechanism of photosynthesis and stomatal transpiration
Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration in yeast, muscle cells, and mitochondria
Trace double circulation through the human heart, arteries, veins, and capillaries
Explain the filtration and selective reabsorption mechanism inside nephrons of the kidney

concepts.title: Photosynthesis & Autotrophic Nutrition
concepts.description: Light absorption by chlorophyll, splitting of water molecules, and reduction of CO2 into glucose.
concepts.learningOutcome: Explain the inputs, steps, and byproduct release during photosynthesis.

concepts.title: Double Circulation in Humans & Heart Structure
concepts.description: Separate systemic and pulmonary pathways preventing oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mixing.
concepts.learningOutcome: Trace blood flow through auricles, ventricles, pulmonary artery, and aorta.

chapters.subject: English
chapters.title: Grammar: Reported Speech & Subject-Verb Concord
chapters.introduction: Class X CBSE English curriculum requires rigorous precision in reporting dialogues (direct to indirect speech) across assertions, imperatives, interrogatives, and exclamations, alongside rule-governed subject-verb agreement.
learningObjectives: Convert direct statements, questions, and commands into reported speech with accurate tense backshifting
Apply changes in pronouns, time expressions, and reporting verbs (said -> told, asked, commanded)
Ensure subject-verb concord in collective nouns, plural forms with singular meanings, and indefinite pronouns

concepts.title: Tense Backshifting & Pronoun Transformation in Reported Speech
concepts.description: Systematic transformation of present tenses to past tenses when the reporting verb is in the past.
concepts.learningOutcome: Convert dialogue excerpts into error-free reported paragraphs.

concepts.title: Subject-Verb Concord Rules & Exceptions
concepts.description: Rules governing compound subjects, neither/nor, either/or, and collective nouns.
concepts.learningOutcome: Select singular or plural verb forms based on formal agreement rules.

chapters.subject: Social Science
chapters.title: Nationalism in India (History)
chapters.introduction: Explore the growth of modern nationalism in India: the First World War context, Satyagraha and the Rowlatt Act, the Non-Cooperation Movement across cities, countryside, and plantations, the Simon Commission, the Civil Disobedience Movement, the Salt March, and the sense of collective belonging.
learningObjectives: Trace how the First World War created new economic and political conditions in India
Analyze the philosophy of Satyagraha championed by Mahatma Gandhi
Examine the Rowlatt Act, the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, and the Non-Cooperation movement
Compare Civil Disobedience with Non-Cooperation and explain the historic Salt March

concepts.title: Non-Cooperation Movement & Khilafat Movement
concepts.description: Boycott of foreign cloth, courts, and government schools; the alliance between Congress and Khilafat leaders.
concepts.learningOutcome: Explain reasons for launching and later calling off the Non-Cooperation Movement.

chapters.subject: Physical Science
chapters.title: Refraction of Light at Curved Surfaces
chapters.introduction: SCERT Telangana Class X Physical Science: Refraction through spherical lenses (convex and concave), center of curvature, focal length, ray diagrams, lens formula (1/f = 1/v - 1/u), magnification, and power of a lens.
learningObjectives: Construct standard ray diagrams for convex and concave lenses with different object positions
Apply the lens formula and sign convention to calculate image distance, height, and magnification
Determine the power of a lens in dioptres (P = 1/f in meters)

concepts.title: Lens Formula & Cartesian Sign Convention
concepts.description: Applying 1/f = 1/v - 1/u with strict sign discipline for real vs virtual images.
concepts.learningOutcome: Calculate image position and magnification for converging and diverging lenses.

chapters.subject: English
chapters.title: Personality Development (Attitude is Altitude)
chapters.introduction: SCERT Telangana Class X English Reader Unit 1: The inspiring life story of Nick Vujicic, overcoming phocomelia with resilience, determination, and positive mindset. Reading comprehension, prepositional phrases, and speech writing.
learningObjectives: Analyze the central theme of overcoming adversity through positive psychological attitude
Extract inferences and contextual meanings from biographical narrative text
Master prepositional phrases (e.g. in spite of, by means of, in addition to)

concepts.title: Contextual Reading Comprehension & Prepositional Phrases
concepts.description: Analyzing narrative voice, character motivations, and compound prepositions.
concepts.learningOutcome: Answer analytical comprehension questions and apply prepositional idioms accurately.

chapters.subject: Chemistry
chapters.title: Periodic Table, Periodic Properties and Variations
chapters.introduction: ICSE Class 10 Chemistry Chapter 1: Modern Periodic Law, groups and periods, and periodic trends in atomic size, ionization potential, electron affinity, electronegativity, metallic, and non-metallic characters.
learningObjectives: Explain periodic trends across a period (left to right) and down a group (top to bottom)
Relate nuclear charge and number of shells to changes in atomic radius and electronegativity
Predict chemical reactivity and oxide character based on element position in the periodic table

concepts.title: Periodic Trends: Ionization Energy, Electronegativity & Atomic Radius
concepts.description: How nuclear pull and screening effect determine periodic property variations.
concepts.learningOutcome: Arrange elements in increasing or decreasing order of non-metallic character and ionization potential.

chapters.subject: Biology
chapters.title: Cell Cycle, Cell Division & Chromosome Structure
chapters.introduction: ICSE Class 10 Biology Chapter 1: Chromatin network, chromosome structure (centromere, chromatids, genes), cell cycle phases (Interphase: G1, S, G2), Mitosis stages (Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase), and significance of Meiosis.
learningObjectives: Describe the molecular organization of DNA wrapped around histone octamers to form nucleosomes
Identify stages of mitosis from microscopic diagrams based on chromosome alignment and movement
Explain the genetic significance of crossing over during Meiosis in gamete formation

concepts.title: Stages of Mitosis & Diagrammatic Identification
concepts.description: Prophase, Metaphase (equatorial plate alignment), Anaphase (centromere division), and Telophase.
concepts.learningOutcome: Identify and label mitotic phases and differentiate animal vs plant cytokinesis.

chapters.subject: English
chapters.title: Grammar: Transformation of Sentences & Synthesis
chapters.introduction: ICSE English Language Paper 1 Question 5: Advanced sentence transformation without changing meaning. Rephrasing sentences using "No sooner... than", "Hardly... when", "Unless", "Too... to", active/passive, and combining simple sentences into complex or compound sentences.
learningObjectives: Transform affirmative sentences into negative, interrogative, and exclamatory without altering meaning
Master correlative conjunctions: No sooner had... than, Hardly had... when, Scarcely... when
Synthesize pairs of sentences using participles, infinitives, noun clauses, and absolute phrases

concepts.title: Inversion Structures (No sooner / Hardly) & Sentence Synthesis
concepts.description: Using auxiliary inversion with negative adverbials to combine and transform sentences.
concepts.learningOutcome: Transform sentences accurately following strict ICSE Paper 1 grammar conventions.

chapters.subject: English
chapters.title: Grammar: Tenses, Aspects & Modals
chapters.introduction: Class VIII NCERT English: Present, past, and future time aspects (simple, continuous, perfect, perfect continuous) and modal auxiliaries expressing ability, permission, obligation, possibility, and deduction.
learningObjectives: Differentiate past simple and present perfect in time-bound contexts
Select appropriate modal verbs: can, could, may, might, must, should, ought to
Identify and correct errors of verb forms in continuous writing

concepts.title: Present Perfect vs Simple Past & Modal Logic
concepts.description: Using "since/for" with present perfect and specific past time markers with simple past.
concepts.learningOutcome: Fill blanks with correct verb forms and modal auxiliaries.

chapters.subject: Social Science
chapters.title: Resources: Types & Sustainable Development (Geography)
chapters.introduction: NCERT Class VIII Geography Chapter 1: Definition of a resource, utility and value, classification into natural (renewable vs non-renewable), human-made, and human resources, resource conservation, and the principles of sustainable development.
learningObjectives: Define resource and understand the role of human technology in transforming natural gifts into resources
Distinguish renewable (solar, wind) and non-renewable (fossil fuels, minerals) resources
Explain sustainable development: balancing the need to use resources and conserving them for the future

concepts.title: Renewable vs Non-Renewable Resources & Sustainability Principles
concepts.description: Conservation ethics and the 3Rs (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) in resource management.
concepts.learningOutcome: Categorize resources and suggest practical conservation practices.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Components of Food (Nutrients & Balanced Diet)
chapters.introduction: NCERT Class VI Science: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, dietary fibre (roughage), and water. Laboratory tests for starch, protein, and fats, balanced diet, and deficiency diseases.
learningObjectives: Identify major nutrients in different foods and their biological roles
Describe chemical tests using iodine (for starch), copper sulphate & caustic soda (for proteins)
Explain deficiency diseases: scurvy, rickets, beriberi, anemia, and goitre

concepts.title: Nutrient Tests & Deficiency Diseases
concepts.description: Conducting chemical tests and recognizing deficiency disorders from symptoms.
concepts.learningOutcome: Connect specific vitamin/mineral deficiencies with their characteristic diseases.

chapters.subject: English
chapters.title: Nouns, Pronouns and Sentence Construction
chapters.introduction: Foundational English grammar for Class VI: proper, common, collective, and abstract nouns; personal, possessive, and demonstrative pronouns; and subject-predicate structure.
learningObjectives: Classify nouns into abstract, collective, proper, and common categories
Use pronouns correctly to avoid repetitive noun usage
Construct complete, punctuated sentences with matching subjects and predicates

concepts.title: Noun Classification & Pronoun Replacement
concepts.description: Identifying noun classes and applying correct pronoun agreement in sentences.
concepts.learningOutcome: Identify abstract nouns and replace subject phrases with accurate pronouns.

chapters.subject: English
chapters.title: Grammar: Adverbs – Types, Usage & Sentence Placement
chapters.introduction: An adverb is a word that modifies, clarifies, or qualifies a verb, an adjective, or another adverb. Adverbs express manner (how), time (when), place (where), frequency (how often), and degree (to what extent). In this comprehensive module, students master adverbial identification, structural formation, syntactic placement, and avoiding adjective-adverb confusion in formal communication.
learningObjectives: Define adverbs and understand why they are used to add precision, nuance, and vivid detail
Distinguish between adjectives (modifying nouns/pronouns) and adverbs (modifying verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs)
Classify adverbs into five primary categories: Manner, Time, Place, Frequency, and Degree
Apply correct syntactic word order and placement rules (especially adverbs of frequency with auxiliary vs main verbs)
Form regular and irregular adverbs correctly and avoid common traps such as flat adverbs and false -ly adjectives

concepts.title: Adverbs: Definition, Modification & Adjective vs Adverb Distinction
concepts.description: Understanding how adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, and other adverbs, and differentiating adjectives from adverbs.
concepts.learningOutcome: Identify adverbs in sentences and differentiate them from qualifying adjectives.

concepts.title: Types of Adverbs (Manner, Time, Place, Frequency, Degree) & Sentence Placement
concepts.description: Categorizing adverbs into 5 core types and correctly positioning them before main verbs, after "to be", or at sentence margins.
concepts.learningOutcome: Classify adverbs into 5 types and position frequency/manner adverbs accurately in sentences.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Acids, Bases and Salts
chapters.introduction: Acids and bases are fundamental chemical classifications that define pH, chemical reactivity, and industrial synthesis. In this chapter, we explore indicators, neutralization reactions, the pH scale, and the manufacturing of essential salts like bleaching powder, baking soda, and plaster of Paris.
learningObjectives: Understand chemical properties of acids and bases with metals, carbonates, and oxides
Explain the concept of pH as a measure of hydronium ion concentration
Describe the importance of pH in everyday life (digestive system, soil, tooth decay)
Detail the preparation and uses of sodium hydroxide, bleaching powder, baking soda, washing soda, and plaster of Paris

concepts.title: Properties of Acids & Bases, Indicators and pH Scale
concepts.description: Litmus, synthetic indicators, neutralization reactions, and pH scale interpretation.
concepts.learningOutcome: Interpret pH values and predict acidity, basicity, and neutralization outcomes.

concepts.title: Important Salts & Plaster of Paris Formulation
concepts.description: Preparation, properties, and chemical formulas of industrial and domestic salts.
concepts.learningOutcome: State chemical equations for the preparation of bleaching powder, baking soda, and gypsum.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Metals and Non-metals
chapters.introduction: Elements are categorized as metals and non-metals based on their electronic configuration, physical ductility/conductivity, and chemical reactivity series. We investigate ionic bonding, extraction of metals from ores (metallurgy), and corrosion prevention.
learningObjectives: Compare physical and chemical properties of metals and non-metals
Explain reactivity series and displacement reactions
Describe the formation and properties of ionic compounds
Understand basic metallurgical processes: roasting, calcination, and electrolytic refining

concepts.title: Reactivity Series & Ionic Compound Formation
concepts.description: Metal displacement reactions, electron transfer, and lattice properties of ionic salts.
concepts.learningOutcome: Predict reaction feasibility using the activity series and draw electron-dot structures.

concepts.title: Metallurgy: Extraction of Metals & Refining
concepts.description: Concentration of ores, calcination, roasting, reduction, and electrolytic refining of copper.
concepts.learningOutcome: Outline extraction steps for metals of low, medium, and high reactivity.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Carbon and its Compounds
chapters.introduction: Carbon displays unique tetravalency and catenation, forming covalent bonds that create millions of organic molecules. We study homologous series, functional groups, IUPAC nomenclature, combustion, addition, substitution reactions, and soaps vs. detergents.
learningObjectives: Explain covalent bonding in carbon, methane, and carbon dioxide
Identify homologous series and functional groups (alcohol, aldehyde, ketone, carboxylic acid)
Write IUPAC names and structural formulas of saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons
Differentiate between soaps and detergents and explain micelle cleaning action

concepts.title: Covalent Bonding, Catenation & Homologous Series
concepts.description: Tetravalency, allotropes of carbon, alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, and functional groups.
concepts.learningOutcome: Identify homologous series members and determine general chemical formulas.

concepts.title: Chemical Reactions of Carbon Compounds & Soaps
concepts.description: Combustion, oxidation, addition reactions with nickel catalyst, esterification, and saponification.
concepts.learningOutcome: Explain saponification and the hydrophilic/hydrophobic structure of soap micelles.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Control and Coordination
chapters.introduction: Organisms respond to stimuli through nervous and hormonal coordination. In animals, neurons, reflex arcs, the central nervous system, and endocrine glands govern homeostasis. In plants, phytohormones regulate tropic and nastic movements.
learningObjectives: Describe the structure and function of a neuron and synapse
Explain the reflex arc mechanism and components of human brain
Identify plant hormones (auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, abscisic acid) and tropic movements
Outline endocrine glands, hormones secreted, and feedback mechanisms

concepts.title: Nervous System, Synapse Transmission & Reflex Arcs
concepts.description: Electrical impulses in neurons, neurotransmitter diffusion across synapses, and reflex pathways.
concepts.learningOutcome: Trace the impulse path from sensory receptor to effector organ in a reflex arc.

concepts.title: Plant Hormones & Animal Endocrine Glands
concepts.description: Phototropism, geotropism, auxin differential elongation, thyroxine, insulin, and adrenaline.
concepts.learningOutcome: Correlate endocrine hormone functions with deficiency and excess symptoms.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Light – Reflection and Refraction
chapters.introduction: Light travels in straight lines and exhibits reflection and refraction when encountering optical boundaries. We master spherical mirrors (concave and convex), the mirror formula, magnification, Snell’s law of refraction, lenses, and power of a lens in dioptres.
learningObjectives: Draw ray diagrams for concave and convex mirrors across various object positions
Apply mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u and calculate magnification
State laws of refraction and Snell’s law: sin(i)/sin(r) = constant
Apply lens formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u and calculate optical power P = 1/f

concepts.title: Reflection at Spherical Mirrors & Mirror Formula
concepts.description: Focal length, center of curvature, ray tracing, Cartesian sign convention, and magnification.
concepts.learningOutcome: Solve numerical problems using the mirror formula with correct signs.

concepts.title: Refraction, Snell’s Law, Lens Formula & Optical Power
concepts.description: Refractive index, convex/concave lens image formation, lens formula, and power P = 1/f (m).
concepts.learningOutcome: Calculate refractive indices and lens power in dioptres for optical combinations.

chapters.subject: Science
chapters.title: Electricity
chapters.introduction: Electric charge flow constitutes electric current. In this chapter, we study electric potential difference, Ohm’s law, electrical resistance and resistivity, resistors in series and parallel, heating effect of electric current (Joule’s law), and electric power.
learningObjectives: Define electric current (I = Q/t) and potential difference (V = W/Q)
Verify Ohm’s law V = IR and understand factors affecting resistance (R = ρl/A)
Calculate equivalent resistance for series and parallel combinations
Apply Joule’s law of heating (H = I^2 R t) and compute electric power and commercial energy units (kWh)

concepts.title: Ohm’s Law, Resistance & Resistivity Factors
concepts.description: Current, potential difference, V-I graphs, and resistivity dependence on length and area.
concepts.learningOutcome: Compute resistance changes when wires are stretched or doubled in area.

concepts.title: Resistors in Series/Parallel, Joule’s Heating & Power
concepts.description: Equivalent resistances, current division, voltage division, heating effect, and electric power.
concepts.learningOutcome: Solve complex circuit combinations and compute electricity consumption costs.

chapters.subject: Physical Science
chapters.title: Structure of Atom (Bohr-Sommerfeld Model & Quantum Numbers)
chapters.introduction: Understanding the atomic structure is fundamental to modern chemistry and physics. We explore electromagnetic spectrum, Bohr’s atomic model, Sommerfeld elliptical orbits, quantum numbers (n, l, ml, ms), Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion principle, and Hund’s rule of maximum multiplicity.
learningObjectives: Explain electromagnetic wave parameters: wavelength, frequency, wave number, and velocity
Explain the significance of the four quantum numbers in defining electron states
Apply Aufbau principle, Pauli’s exclusion principle, and Hund’s rule to write electronic configurations
Differentiate between degenerate orbitals and orbital shapes (s, p, d)

concepts.title: Quantum Numbers & Electronic Configuration Principles
concepts.description: Principal (n), Azimuthal (l), Magnetic (ml), and Spin (ms) quantum numbers and orbital filling rules.
concepts.learningOutcome: Assign quantum numbers to electrons and write correct electronic configurations for elements 1-30.

chapters.subject: Physical Science
chapters.title: Chemical Bonding (Lewis Theory & Octet Rule)
chapters.introduction: Atoms bond to achieve stable electronic noble-gas configurations. We explore ionic bonding (electrostatic attraction between ions), covalent bonding (electron sharing), polar vs nonpolar bonds, and properties of ionic and covalent substances.
learningObjectives: Explain ionic bond formation in NaCl and MgCl2 using Lewis dot structures
Explain covalent bond formation in H2, O2, N2, and CH4
Contrast ionic compounds (high melting points, conduct in solution) with covalent molecules

concepts.title: Ionic & Covalent Bond Formation & Properties
concepts.description: Electron transfer, electron sharing, lattice energy, and conductivity differences.
concepts.learningOutcome: Represent chemical bond formation with Lewis electron-dot diagrams.

chapters.subject: Physical Science
chapters.title: Electric Current & Kirchhoff’s Laws
chapters.introduction: Electric current in metallic conductors involves drift velocity of free electrons. We explore drift speed, electric potential, Ohm’s law, Kirchhoff’s Junction Law, Kirchhoff’s Loop Law, and electric power dissipation.
learningObjectives: Define drift velocity (vd = I / nAe) and understand internal resistance of cells
State and apply Kirchhoff’s Junction Law (Conservation of Charge)
State and apply Kirchhoff’s Loop Law (Conservation of Energy)

concepts.title: Kirchhoff’s Laws & Circuit Analysis
concepts.description: Junction law, loop law, and sign conventions in multi-loop electrical circuits.
concepts.learningOutcome: Calculate branch currents and potential differences across complex network nodes.

chapters.subject: Biological Science
chapters.title: Nutrition – Food Supplying System
chapters.introduction: All living organisms need nutrition to carry out vital functions. We explore autotrophic nutrition (photosynthesis, Hill’s reaction, light and dark reactions in chloroplasts), heterotrophic nutrition, human digestive system, and nutritional deficiency diseases (Kwashiorkor, Marasmus).
learningObjectives: Describe the photochemical and biosynthetic phases of photosynthesis
Explain experiments showing requirement of chlorophyll, light, and CO2 for starch production
Trace food passage and enzyme actions throughout the human alimentary canal
Identify malnutrition diseases and dietary solutions

concepts.title: Photosynthesis Mechanism & Human Digestive Enzymes
concepts.description: Light-dependent reaction in grana thylakoids, Calvin cycle in stroma, and digestive enzyme functions.
concepts.learningOutcome: Explain the role of chlorophyll, ATP, and NADPH in photosynthesis and digestive enzymes in nutrient absorption.

chapters.subject: Biological Science
chapters.title: Respiration – The Energy Releasing System
chapters.introduction: Respiration releases chemical energy stored in glucose via aerobic and anaerobic pathways. We study respiratory passage in humans, gaseous exchange at alveolar and tissue levels, glycolysis, Krebs cycle, and fermentation in yeast.
learningObjectives: Differentiate between aerobic cellular respiration and anaerobic fermentation
Explain alveolar gas exchange by partial pressure gradients
Describe ATP generation and energy yield differences

concepts.title: Cellular Respiration Pathways & Gas Exchange Mechanisms
concepts.description: Glycolysis in cytoplasm, Krebs cycle in mitochondrial matrix, lactic acid vs ethanol fermentation.
concepts.learningOutcome: Compare energy outputs and chemical end products of aerobic vs anaerobic respiration.

chapters.subject: Chemistry
chapters.title: Mole Concept and Stoichiometry (Gay-Lussac & Avogadro Laws)
chapters.introduction: Quantitative chemistry relies on the mole concept and gas volume relations. In this chapter, we master Gay-Lussac’s Law of Combining Volumes, Avogadro’s Law, molar volume at STP (22.4 dm³), vapour density (VD = MW/2), empirical and molecular formula calculations, and stoichiometry.
learningObjectives: Apply Gay-Lussac’s Law to determine reacting gas volumes and excess gases
Relate molecular weight to relative vapour density: MW = 2 x VD
Calculate percentage composition, empirical formula, and molecular formula
Solve stoichiometric mass-mass and mass-volume equations at standard temperature and pressure

concepts.title: Gay-Lussac’s Law & Avogadro’s Hypothesis
concepts.description: Gas volume ratios, molar volume at STP, and Avogadro number calculations.
concepts.learningOutcome: Solve volume-volume stoichiometry problems at STP under Gay-Lussac’s law.

concepts.title: Empirical & Molecular Formula & Vapour Density
concepts.description: Determining empirical formulas from percent compositions and molecular formulas using vapour density.
concepts.learningOutcome: Calculate the molecular formula of an organic compound given its elemental analysis and vapour density.

chapters.subject: Chemistry
chapters.title: Electrolysis (Preferential Discharge & Industrial Applications)
chapters.introduction: Electrolysis is the decomposition of a chemical compound in molten or aqueous state by passage of direct electric current. We study electrolytes vs non-electrolytes, preferential discharge of ions based on electrochemical series, electrolysis of molten lead bromide, acidified water, and copper sulphate with inert and active electrodes, electroplating, and electrorefining.
learningObjectives: State the selective discharge criteria for cations and anions
Write half-cell electrode reactions at cathode (reduction) and anode (oxidation)
Explain electroplating of an iron spoon with nickel or silver
Describe electrolytic refining of blister copper

concepts.title: Electrochemical Preferential Discharge & Half-Reactions
concepts.description: Factors determining ion discharge (position in series, concentration, electrode nature).
concepts.learningOutcome: Write balanced oxidation and reduction half-cell equations for various electrolytic cells.

lessons.title: Addition & Subtraction of Unlike Fractions (LCM Method)

explanation.en: When adding or subtracting fractions with unlike denominators, you CANNOT simply add the denominators together! For example, 1/2 + 1/3 is NOT 2/5. You must first find the Least Common Denominator (LCM of denominators), convert each fraction into an equivalent fraction with that common denominator, and only then combine the numerators.
explanation.hi: जब असमान हर (denominators) वाले भिन्न (fractions) जोड़े या घटाए जाते हैं, तो हरों को सीधे नहीं जोड़ा जा सकता! उदाहरण के लिए, 1/2 + 1/3 का मान 2/5 नहीं होता। आपको पहले हरों का लघुत्तम समापवर्त्य (LCM) ज्ञात करना होगा, प्रत्येक भिन्न को समान हर वाले तुल्य भिन्न में बदलना होगा, और फिर अंशों (numerators) को जोड़ना होगा।
explanation.te: వేర్వేరు హారాలు (denominators) కలిగిన భిన్నాలను కూడేటప్పుడు లేదా తీసివేసేటప్పుడు, హారాలను నేరుగా కూడకూడదు! ఉదాహరణకు, 1/2 + 1/3 అనేది 2/5 కాదు. ముందుగా హారాల క.సా.గు (LCM) కనుగొని, ప్రతి భిన్నాన్ని సమాన హారంగల సమాన భిన్నంగా మార్చి, ఆ తర్వాతే లవాలను (numerators) కూడాలి.

definition.en: The smallest positive integer that is divisible by all the denominators in the fraction set.
definition.hi: वह सबसे छोटी धनात्मक संख्या जो दिए गए सभी भिन्नों के हरों से पूर्णतः विभाजित होती है।
definition.te: ఇచ్చిన అన్ని భిన్నాల హారాలచే నిశ్శేషంగా భాగించబడే అతిచిన్న ధనాత్మక పూర్ణాంకం.

definition.en: Fractions that represent the exact same value or proportion, obtained by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same non-zero integer.
definition.hi: वे भिन्न जो समान मान या अनुपात दर्शाते हैं, जिन्हें अंश और हर को समान गैर-शून्य संख्या से गुणा या भाग करके प्राप्त किया जाता है।
definition.te: లవం మరియు హారాన్ని ఒకే శూన్యేతర సంఖ్యతో గుణించడం లేదా భాగించడం ద్వారా పొందే సమాన విలువ గల భిన్నాలు.

stepByStep.en: Step 1: Check denominators. They are 3 and 4 (unlike denominators).
stepByStep.hi: चरण 1: हरों की जाँच करें। वे 3 और 4 हैं (असमान हर)।
stepByStep.te: దశ 1: హారాలను గమనించండి. అవి 3 మరియు 4 (విభిన్న హారాలు).

stepByStep.en: Step 2: Find LCM of 3 and 4. Since 3 and 4 have no common factors other than 1, LCM = 3 × 4 = 12.
stepByStep.hi: चरण 2: 3 और 4 का LCM निकालें। LCM = 3 × 4 = 12।

stepByStep.en: Step 3: Convert to equivalent fractions with denominator 12: (2×4)/(3×4) = 8/12, and (3×3)/(4×3) = 9/12.
Step 4: Keep the denominator 12, add only the numerators: (8 + 9) / 12 = 17/12.

keyInsight.en: Never add 2+3 over 3+4! Denominators define the slice size; you must equalize slice sizes before counting.
keyInsight.hi: कभी भी (2+3)/(3+4) न करें! हर केवल टुकड़ों का आकार बताता है।
keyInsight.te: ఎప్పటికీ (2+3)/(3+4) అని రాయకండి! హారం కేవలం భాగాన్ని సూచిస్తుంది.

correction.en: Always convert both to equivalent fractions having a common denominator: 8/12 + 9/12 = 17/12.
correction.hi: हमेशा समान हर वाले तुल्य भिन्न बनाएं: 8/12 + 9/12 = 17/12।
correction.te: ఎల్లప్పుడూ ఉమ్మడి హారంగల సమాన భిన్నాలుగా మార్చండి: 8/12 + 9/12 = 17/12.

whyItHappens.en: Intuitive carryover from whole number addition without understanding that the denominator represents unit scale, not count.
whyItHappens.hi: पूर्णांकों के जोड़ की आदत, यह समझे बिना कि हर इकाई का पैमाना है न कि गिनती।
whyItHappens.te: హారం అనేది కొలత యూనిట్ అని గమనించకుండా సాధారణ సంఖ్యల వలె కూడడం వల్ల.

summaryPoints.en: 1. Denominators represent the division of a unit; numerators represent the count.
summaryPoints.hi: 1. हर किसी इकाई के विभाजन को दर्शाता है; अंश गणना को दर्शाता है।
summaryPoints.te: 1. హారం విభజించబడిన భాగాలను, లవం తీసుకున్న భాగాలను తెలుపుతుంది.

summaryPoints.en: 2. To add/subtract unlike fractions: Find LCM -> Form equivalent fractions -> Add numerators -> Simplify.
summaryPoints.hi: 2. असमान भिन्नों के लिए: LCM निकालें -> तुल्य भिन्न बनाएं -> अंश जोड़ें -> सरल करें।
summaryPoints.te: 2. విభిన్న భిన్నాలకు: క.సా.గు కనుగొనండి -> సమాన భిన్నాలు రాయండి -> లవాలు కూడండి -> కనిష్ట రూపం.

explanation.en: Transposition is a quick method derived from the golden rule of equations: "Whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other." When a term moves from one side of the equal sign (=) to the other, its operation inverts: + becomes -, - becomes +, × becomes ÷, and ÷ becomes ×.
explanation.hi: पक्षांतरण (Transposition) समीकरणों के मूल नियम पर आधारित है: "जो क्रिया एक तरफ करें, वही दूसरी तरफ भी करें।" जब कोई पद बराबर (=) के दूसरी तरफ जाता है, तो उसका चिन्ह बदल जाता है: + बनता है -, - बनता है +, × बनता है ÷, और ÷ बनता है ×।
explanation.te: పక్షాంతరీకరణ (Transposition) అనేది సమీకరణాల ప్రాథమిక నియమంపై ఆధారపడి ఉంటుంది. సమానత్వ గుర్తు (=) దాటినప్పుడు ప్రతి ప్రక్రియ విలోమమవుతుంది: + కాస్తా - అవుతుంది, - కాస్తా + అవుతుంది, గుణకారం భాగాహారమవుతుంది.

definition.en: The algebraic operation of transferring a term from one side of an equation to the other while altering its sign.
definition.hi: किसी पद को चिन्ह बदलकर समीकरण के एक पक्ष से दूसरे पक्ष में ले जाने की प्रक्रिया।
definition.te: సమీకరణంలో ఒక వైపు ఉన్న పదాన్ని గుర్తు మార్చి మరొక వైపుకు తరలించే ప్రక్రియ.

stepByStep.en: Step 1: Isolate the variable term (3x). Move the constant (-7) to the RHS.
stepByStep.hi: चरण 1: चर पद (3x) को अलग करें। -7 को दाईं तरफ ले जाएं।
stepByStep.te: దశ 1: చరరాశి పదాన్ని (3x) వేరు చేయండి. -7 ను కుడివైపుకు తరలించండి.

stepByStep.en: Step 2: Sign rule: When -7 moves across =, it becomes +7. So: 3x = 14 + 7.
stepByStep.hi: चरण 2: चिन्ह नियम: जब -7 दाईं ओर जाएगा तो +7 बनेगा। 3x = 14 + 7 = 21।

stepByStep.en: Step 3: Now isolate x. Since 3 multiplies x, it transposes as division: x = 21 / 3 = 7.
stepByStep.hi: चरण 3: अब x का मान निकालें: x = 21 / 3 = 7।
stepByStep.te: దశ 3: 3 అనేది x ని గుణిస్తోంది కాబట్టి భాగిస్తుంది: x = 21 / 3 = 7.

stepByStep.en: Step 4: Verify by substituting x=7 back: 3(7) - 7 = 21 - 7 = 14. LHS = RHS!

keyInsight.en: Never keep the minus sign when moving across the equals sign! 3x = 14 - 7 is a fatal error.
keyInsight.hi: बराबर का चिन्ह पार करते समय चिन्ह बदलना न भूलें! 3x = 14 - 7 लिखना गलत है।
keyInsight.te: = గుర్తు దాటినప్పుడు గుర్తు మార్చడం మర్చిపోకూడదు! 3x = 14 - 7 అని రాయడం తప్పు.

correction.en: When -7 moves to the other side, it MUST invert to +7: 3x = 14 + 7 = 21.
correction.hi: जब -7 दूसरी तरफ जाएगा, तो यह +7 में बदलेगा: 3x = 14 + 7 = 21।

whyItHappens.en: Students mechanically copy the number without executing the inverse operation required to maintain equality.
whyItHappens.hi: समानता बनाए रखने के लिए आवश्यक विपरीत संक्रिया को लागू किए बिना संख्या को वैसे ही लिख देना।
whyItHappens.te: సమీకరణ సమానత్వం కాపాడటానికి విలోమ ప్రక్రియ చేయాలనే అవగాహన లోపించడం వల్ల.

summaryPoints.en: 1. Golden Rule of Equations: The equality balance must be maintained at every step.
summaryPoints.hi: 1. समीकरण का स्वर्णिम नियम: संतुलन हर चरण में बना रहना चाहिए।
summaryPoints.te: 1. సమీకరణాల స్వర్ణ నియమం: ప్రతి దశలో సమతూకం ఉండాలి.

summaryPoints.hi: 2. पक्षांतरण संक्रिया को उलट देता है: + <-> - तथा × <-> ÷।

lessons.title: Balancing Chemical Equations & Law of Conservation of Mass

explanation.en: According to the Law of Conservation of Mass, the total mass of the reactants must equal the total mass of the products. Consequently, the total number of atoms of each individual element on the left-hand side (LHS) must strictly equal the number of atoms on the right-hand side (RHS). To achieve this, you place whole-number stoichiometric coefficients directly in front of the chemical formulas. You must NEVER modify subscript numbers inside a chemical formula (e.g., changing H2O to H2O2 is forbidden because H2O2 is hydrogen peroxide, a toxic antiseptic bleach, not water!).
explanation.hi: द्रव्यमान संरक्षण के नियम के अनुसार, अभिकारकों का कुल द्रव्यमान उत्पादों के कुल द्रव्यमान के बराबर होना चाहिए। अतः दोनों ओर प्रत्येक तत्व के परमाणुओं की संख्या बराबर होनी चाहिए। इसके लिए सूत्र के आगे पूर्ण गुणांक (coefficients) लगाए जाते हैं। सूत्र के भीतर के पादांक (subscript) को कभी न बदलें!
explanation.te: ద్రవ్య నిత్యత్వ నియమం ప్రకారం క్రియాజనకాల మొత్తం ద్రవ్యరాశి క్రియాజన్యాల మొత్తం ద్రవ్యరాశికి సమానంగా ఉండాలి. బాణం గుర్తుకు ఇరువైపులా ప్రతి మూలకపు పరమాణువుల సంఖ్య సమానంగా ఉండేలా ఫార్ములా ముందు గుణకాలను మాత్రమే చేర్చాలి. ఫార్ములా లోపలి సంఖ్యలను ఎప్పుడూ మార్చరాదు!

definition.en: An unbalanced chemical equation that shows the reactants and products using chemical symbols without equalizing atom counts.
definition.hi: एक असंतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण जो केवल अभिकारकों और उत्पादों के सूत्रों को दर्शाता है।
definition.te: పరమాణువుల సంఖ్య సమానంగా లేని ప్రాథమిక రసాయన సమీకరణం.

definition.en: A whole number written in front of a chemical formula indicating the relative number of molecules or moles reacting or produced.
definition.hi: रासायनिक सूत्र के आगे लिखी जाने वाली पूर्ण संख्या जो अणुओं या मोल्स की संख्या दर्शाती है।
definition.te: రసాయన చర్యలో పాల్గొనే లేదా ఏర్పడే అణువుల నిష్పత్తిని తెలిపే గుణకం.

problem.en: Balance the reaction of heated iron with steam: Fe(s) + H2O(g) -> Fe3O4(s) + H2(g)
problem.hi: लाल तप्त लोहे की भाप के साथ अभिक्रिया को संतुलित करें: Fe(s) + H2O(g) -> Fe3O4(s) + H2(g)
problem.te: ఇనుము నీటి ఆవిరితో జరిపే చర్యను తుల్యం చేయండి: Fe(s) + H2O(g) -> Fe3O4(s) + H2(g)

stepByStep.en: Step 1 (Atom Inventory): LHS has 1 Fe, 2 H, 1 O. RHS has 3 Fe, 2 H, 4 O. Oxygen has greatest imbalance (1 vs 4).
stepByStep.hi: चरण 1: बाएं पक्ष में 1 Fe, 2 H, 1 O है; दाएं पक्ष में 3 Fe, 2 H, 4 O है।
stepByStep.te: దశ 1: ఎడమవైపు 1 Fe, 2 H, 1 O; కుడివైపు 3 Fe, 2 H, 4 O ఉన్నాయి.

stepByStep.en: Step 2 (Balance Oxygen): Place coefficient 4 in front of H2O: Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + H2. Oxygen is now 4 on both sides.
stepByStep.hi: चरण 2: H2O के आगे 4 लगाएं: Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + H2। ऑक्सीजन संतुलित हो गया।
stepByStep.te: దశ 2: H2O ముందు 4 ఉంచండి: Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + H2. ఆక్సిజన్ తుల్యమైంది.

stepByStep.en: Step 3 (Balance Hydrogen): LHS now has 4 x 2 = 8 H atoms. Place 4 in front of H2 on RHS: Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2.
stepByStep.hi: चरण 3: बाएं 8 हाइड्रोजन हैं। दाएं H2 के आगे 4 लगाएं: Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2।
stepByStep.te: దశ 3: ఎడమవైపు 8 H లు ఉన్నాయి. కుడివైపు H2 ముందు 4 ఉంచండి: Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2.

stepByStep.en: Step 4 (Balance Iron): RHS has 3 Fe atoms. Place 3 in front of Fe on LHS: 3Fe(s) + 4H2O(g) -> Fe3O4(s) + 4H2(g).
stepByStep.hi: चरण 4: दाएं 3 Fe हैं। बाएं Fe के आगे 3 लगाएं: 3Fe(s) + 4H2O(g) -> Fe3O4(s) + 4H2(g)।
stepByStep.te: దశ 4: కుడివైపు 3 Fe లు ఉన్నాయి. ఎడమవైపు Fe ముందు 3 ఉంచండి: 3Fe(s) + 4H2O(g) -> Fe3O4(s) + 4H2(g).

keyInsight.en: Check: Fe: 3=3, H: 8=8, O: 4=4. All atoms conserved. State symbols reflect iron metal and water vapor.
keyInsight.hi: जाँच: Fe: 3=3, H: 8=8, O: 4=4। द्रव्यमान पूर्णतः संरक्षित है।
keyInsight.te: తనిఖీ: Fe: 3=3, H: 8=8, O: 4=4. అన్ని పరమాణువులు సమానమయ్యాయి.

mistake.en: Writing subscripts to balance atoms: e.g., H2 + O2 -> H2O2 to balance oxygen.
mistake.hi: ऑक्सीजन संतुलित करने के लिए H2 + O2 -> H2O2 लिखना।
mistake.te: ఆక్సిజన్ తుల్యం చేయడానికి H2O2 అని ఫార్ములా మార్చడం.

correction.en: Subscripts alter compound identity (H2O2 is toxic hydrogen peroxide, not water). Write 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O.
correction.hi: H2O2 हाइड्रोजन परॉक्साइड है, जल नहीं। सही रूप 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O है।
correction.te: H2O2 అంటే హైడ్రోజన్ పెరాక్సైడ్, నీరు కాదు. సరైన సమీకరణం: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O.

whyItHappens.en: Students forget that chemical formulas represent fixed molecular bonds governed by valency.
whyItHappens.hi: छात्र भूल जाते हैं कि रासायनिक सूत्र संयोजकता से बंधे होते हैं।
whyItHappens.te: రసాయన సూత్రాలు స్థిర బంధాలతో ఏర్పడతాయని విద్యార్థులు మరిచిపోవడం.

summaryPoints.en: Total mass and individual atomic counts are invariant across any closed chemical reaction.
summaryPoints.hi: किसी भी बंद रासायनिक क्रिया में कुल द्रव्यमान और प्रत्येक परमाणु की संख्या स्थिर रहती है।
summaryPoints.te: రసాయన చర్యకు ముందు మరియు తరువాత మొత్తం ద్రవ్యరాశి మరియు పరమాణువుల సంఖ్య మారదు.

topicIntroduction.en: A chemical reaction represents the transformation of reactants into products. Because atoms are indivisible in chemical transformations, balancing equations is the foundational skill of all chemistry.
topicIntroduction.hi: रासायनिक अभिक्रिया अभिकारकों के उत्पादों में रूपांतरण को दर्शाती है। चूँकि परमाणु रासायनिक क्रियाओं में न तो नष्ट होते हैं और न बनते हैं, समीकरण को संतुलित करना रसायन विज्ञान का आधार है।
topicIntroduction.te: రసాయన చర్య అనేది క్రియాజనకాలు క్రియాజన్యాలుగా మారే ప్రక్రియను సూచిస్తుంది. రసాయన చర్యల్లో పరమాణువులు నాశనం కావు కాబట్టి సమీకరణాలను తుల్యం చేయడం రసాయన శాస్త్రానికి పునాది.

whyLearn.en: Mastering chemical balancing enables you to calculate theoretical yields, avoid toxic byproduct oversights in industrial synthesis, and predict exact reagent requirements in laboratories.
whyLearn.hi: रासायनिक संतुलन में निपुणता से आप प्रयोगशालाओं और उद्योगों में पदार्थों की सही मात्रा की गणना कर सकते हैं।
whyLearn.te: రసాయన తుల్యత నేర్చుకోవడం ద్వారా ప్రయోగశాలల్లో మరియు పరిశ్రమల్లో అవసరమైన రసాయనాల పరిమాణాన్ని ఖచ్చితంగా లెక్కించవచ్చు.

learningObjectives: State and apply Antoine Lavoisier's Law of Conservation of Mass to skeletal reactions
Execute the step-by-step hit-and-trial method by prioritizing elements with greatest atomic imbalance
Incorporate mandatory physical state symbols: (s), (l), (g), and (aq) alongside temperature/catalyst notations
Distinguish subscripts (which define molecular identity) from stoichiometric coefficients (which specify molar quantities)

prerequisiteKnowledge.en: Class 9 Dalton's Atomic Theory: Atoms cannot be created, destroyed, or divided during chemical reactions.
prerequisiteKnowledge.hi: कक्षा 9 डॉल्टन का परमाणु सिद्धांत: रासायनिक क्रियाओं में परमाणु अविभाज्य रहते हैं।
prerequisiteKnowledge.te: 9వ తరగతి డాల్టన్ పరమాణు సిద్ధాంతం: రసాయన చర్యల్లో పరమాణువులు సృష్టించబడవు లేదా నాశనం కావు.

prerequisiteKnowledge.en: Chemical formula writing and valency rules for binary compounds and polyatomic ions (e.g., SO4^2-, NO3^-, OH^-).
prerequisiteKnowledge.hi: बहुपरमाणुक आयनों और यौगिकों के रासायनिक सूत्र व संयोजकता नियम।
prerequisiteKnowledge.te: బహుళ పరమాణుక అయాన్లు మరియు సంయోజకత సూత్రాలు.

principlesAndRules.heading: The 4 Golden Rules of Chemical Balancing

rule.en:
1. Enclose chemical formulas in protective boxes; never alter characters inside the box.
2. Count atoms on LHS and RHS in an Atom Inventory Table.
3. Balance the compound containing the maximum number of atoms first (typically Oxygen or polyatomic radicals).
4. Balance elemental metals and gases (like Fe, H2, O2) last.
rule.hi: 1. रासायनिक सूत्रों को कभी न बदलें। 2. दोनों पक्षों के परमाणुओं की सूची बनाएं। 3. सबसे बड़े यौगिक से संतुलन शुरू करें। 4. स्वतंत्र तत्वों को अंत में संतुलित करें।
rule.te: 1. ఫార్ములాలను మార్చకూడదు. 2. ఇరువైపులా పరమాణువులను లెక్కించాలి. 3. ఎక్కువ పరమాణువులు గల పదార్థంతో ప్రారంభించాలి. 4. ఒంటరి మూలకాలను చివరగా తుల్యం చేయాలి.

diagramsAndTables.title: Atom Tabulation Table for Fe + H2O Reaction

description.en: Comparison of initial versus balanced atomic counts across reactants and products.
description.hi: अभिकारकों और उत्पादों के बीच परमाणुओं की तुलना तालिका।

realWorldApplications.en: Automotive Airbags: The rapid decomposition of sodium azide (2NaN3 -> 2Na + 3N2) requires exact stoichiometric balancing to inflate the bag with non-toxic nitrogen gas in 40 milliseconds.
realWorldApplications.hi: कारों के एयरबैग: सोडियम एजाइड का सटीक संतुलित विघटन 40 मिलीसेकंड में नाइट्रोजन गैस भरकर जान बचाता है।
realWorldApplications.te: కారు ఎయిర్‌బ్యాగ్‌లు: సోడియం అజైడ్ ఖచ్చితమైన రసాయన చర్య ద్వారా 40 మిల్లీసెకన్లలో నైట్రోజన్ వాయువును విడుదల చేసి ప్రయాణికులను కాపాడుతుంది.

importantPoints.en: A balanced chemical equation provides quantitative stoichiometric ratios between reactants and products.
importantPoints.hi: संतुलित समीकरण अभिकारकों और उत्पादों के बीच मात्रात्मक अनुपात प्रदान करता है।
importantPoints.te: తుల్య రసాయన సమీకరణం పదార్థాల మధ్య పరిమాణాత్మక నిష్పత్తులను అందిస్తుంది.

importantPoints.en: Always reduce coefficients to the lowest whole-number ratio (e.g. 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O, not 4H2 + 2O2 -> 4H2O).
importantPoints.hi: गुणांकों को हमेशा न्यूनतम पूर्णांक अनुपात में रखें।
importantPoints.te: గుణకాలను ఎల్లప్పుడూ కనిష్ట పూర్ణాంక నిష్పత్తిలో ఉంచాలి.

revisionNotes.en: Step 1: Write correct skeletal formulas. Step 2: Tabulate atom counts. Step 3: Equalize largest atom count first using coefficients. Step 4: Verify all elements and add state symbols.
revisionNotes.hi: कंकाली सूत्र लिखें -> परमाणुओं की गणना करें -> बड़े यौगिक को पहले संतुलित करें -> भौतिक अवस्थाएं लिखें।
revisionNotes.te: ప్రాథమిక సమీకరణం రాయండి -> పరమాణువులను లెక్కించండి -> గుణకాలతో తుల్యం చేయండి -> భౌతిక స్థితులను గుర్తించండి.

topicSummary.en: Balancing chemical equations is an expression of mass invariance. Coefficients scale molecular quantities without modifying molecular structures, enabling precise quantitative chemical analysis.
topicSummary.hi: रासायनिक संतुलन द्रव्यमान संरक्षण का व्यावहारिक रूप है जो अणुओं की संरचना बदले बिना उनकी मात्रा को संतुलित करता है।
topicSummary.te: రసాయన సమీకరణాలను తుల్యం చేయడం అనేది ద్రవ్య నిత్యత్వ నియమానికి ప్రతీక. ఇది పదార్థాల స్వభావాన్ని మార్చకుండా వాటి పరిమాణాలను సమతుల్యం చేస్తుంది.

question.en: What is the coefficient of oxygen in the balanced combustion equation: CH4 + ?O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O?
question.hi: CH4 + ?O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O के संतुलित समीकरण में ऑक्सीजन का गुणांक क्या होगा?
question.te: CH4 + ?O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O తుల్య సమీకరణంలో ఆక్సిజన్ గుణకం ఎంత?

answer.en: Coefficient is 2 (CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O, yielding 4 oxygen atoms on both sides).

quickTip.en: Count product oxygens: 2 from CO2 + 2 from 2H2O = 4 atoms. 4 / 2 = 2 molecules of O2.
quickTip.te: కుడివైపు మొత్తం 4 ఆక్సిజన్ పరమాణువులు ఉన్నాయి కాబట్టి 2 O2 అణువులు అవసరం.

instruction.en: Balance the following neutralization reaction and include physical state symbols:
instruction.hi: निम्नलिखित उदासीनीकरण अभिक्रिया को संतुलित करें और भौतिक अवस्थाएं लिखें:
instruction.te: కింది తటస్థీకరణ చర్యను తుల్యం చేసి భౌతిక స్థితులను రాయండి:

solutionHint.en: Notice NO3 is taken twice in Ca(NO3)2; place 2 in front of HNO3, which produces 2H2O.
solutionHint.hi: Ca(NO3)2 में 2 नाइट्रेट हैं, इसलिए HNO3 के आगे 2 लगाएं।
solutionHint.te: Ca(NO3)2 లో 2 నైట్రేట్లు ఉన్నాయి కాబట్టి 2HNO3 అని రాయాలి.

lessons.title: Reported Speech: Tense Backshifting & Pronoun Transformation

explanation.en: The transformation into reported speech depends fundamentally on the tense of the reporting verb. If the reporting verb is in the present or future tense (e.g. "He says" or "She will say"), the tense inside the reported clause does NOT change. However, when the reporting verb is in the past tense (e.g. "He said", "They told"), the verbs inside undergo a systematic chronological shift one step into the past. Simple Present becomes Simple Past, Present Continuous becomes Past Continuous, and critically, Simple Past shifts to Past Perfect!
explanation.hi: जब रिपोर्टिंग क्रिया भूतकाल में हो ("He said"), तो प्रत्यक्ष कथन का काल एक चरण पीछे चला जाता है: सामान्य वर्तमान -> सामान्य भूतकाल, तथा सामान्य भूतकाल -> पूर्ण भूतकाल! यदि रिपोर्टिंग क्रिया वर्तमान में हो ("He says"), तो काल नहीं बदलता।
explanation.te: రిపోర్టింగ్ వెర్బ్ భూతకాలంలో ("He said") ఉన్నప్పుడు మాత్రమే టెన్స్ వెనక్కి మారుతుంది: Simple Present కాస్త Simple Past గాను, Simple Past కాస్త Past Perfect గాను మారుతుంది. ఒకవేళ రిపోర్టింగ్ వెర్బ్ వర్తమానంలో ("He says") ఉంటే టెన్స్ మారదు.

definition.en: The introductory verb (such as said, asked, exclaimed, stated) that introduces the spoken quotation.
definition.hi: वह क्रिया जो कथन की शुरुआत करती है (जैसे said, told, inquired)।
definition.te: ప్రత్యక్ష వాక్యాన్ని పరిచయం చేసే క్రియ (said, asked, told).

definition.en: The grammatical movement of a verb form into a corresponding past tense when subordinate to a past-tense reporting verb.
definition.hi: भूतकाल की रिपोर्टिंग क्रिया के प्रभाव से मुख्य वाक्य के काल का एक चरण पीछे खिसकना।
definition.te: గతకాలపు రిపోర్టింగ్ వెర్బ్ ప్రభావం వల్ల వాక్యంలోని క్రియ మరింత వెనుకటి కాలంలోకి మారడం.

problem.en: Convert: Arjun said to Priya, "I saw an incredible documentary on lunar exploration yesterday."
problem.hi: परोक्ष कथन में बदलें: Arjun said to Priya, "I saw an incredible documentary on lunar exploration yesterday."
problem.te: ఇండైరెక్ట్ స్పీచ్ లోకి మార్చండి: Arjun said to Priya, "I saw an incredible documentary on lunar exploration yesterday."

stepByStep.en: Step 1: Convert reporting verb with object: "said to Priya" becomes "told Priya that".
stepByStep.hi: चरण 1: "said to Priya" बदलकर "told Priya that" बन जाता है।
stepByStep.te: దశ 1: "said to Priya" కాస్త "told Priya that" గా మారుతుంది.

stepByStep.en: Step 2: Change first-person pronoun: "I" refers to Arjun, so it becomes "he".
stepByStep.hi: चरण 2: सर्वनाम "I" अर्जुन के अनुसार "he" बनता है।
stepByStep.te: దశ 2: "I" అర్జున్‌ను సూచిస్తుంది కాబట్టి "he" అవుతుంది.

stepByStep.en: Step 3: Backshift verb: Simple Past "saw" must shift to Past Perfect "had seen".
stepByStep.hi: चरण 3: Simple Past "saw" बदलकर Past Perfect "had seen" बनेगा।
stepByStep.te: దశ 3: Simple Past "saw" కాస్త Past Perfect "had seen" గా మారుతుంది.

stepByStep.en: Step 4: Shift time adverbial: "yesterday" becomes "the previous day" or "the day before".
stepByStep.hi: चरण 4: समय सूचक "yesterday" बदलकर "the previous day" बनेगा।
stepByStep.te: దశ 4: "yesterday" కాస్త "the previous day" గా మారుతుంది.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: Arjun told Priya that he had seen an incredible documentary on lunar exploration the previous day.

keyInsight.en: Simple past verbs NEVER stay simple past in indirect speech when reporting past events; they always backshift to past perfect (had + V3).
keyInsight.hi: भूतकाल की क्रिया परोक्ष कथन में सदैव Past Perfect (had + V3) में बदलती है।
keyInsight.te: భూతకాలపు క్రియలు ఇండైరెక్ట్ స్పీచ్‌లో ఎల్లప్పుడూ Past Perfect (had + V3) గా మారాలి.

mistake.en: Using "told to": e.g., "Arjun told to Priya that..."
mistake.hi: "told to" का प्रयोग करना: जैसे "Arjun told to Priya..."

correction.en: "Told" is transitive and takes a direct object without "to": "Arjun told Priya that...".
correction.hi: "told" के बाद "to" नहीं लगता: "Arjun told Priya..." सही है।
correction.te: "told" తర్వాత "to" రాదు: "Arjun told Priya that..." సరైనది.

whyItHappens.en: Confusing "said to" (which requires preposition) with "told" (which directly takes an indirect object).
whyItHappens.hi: "said to" और "told" के नियमों में भ्रम।

summaryPoints.en: Subordinating direct quotations to a past reporting verb requires simultaneous transformation of pronouns, tenses, and adverbs.
summaryPoints.hi: प्रत्यक्ष कथन को परोक्ष में बदलते समय सर्वनाम, काल और समय सूचकों का एक साथ ध्यान रखना आवश्यक है।
summaryPoints.te: ఇండైరెక్ట్ స్పీచ్ లోకి మార్చేటప్పుడు సర్వనామాలు, కాలం మరియు సమయ సూచికలు మూడూ మారాలి.

topicIntroduction.en: Direct speech quotes the exact words spoken by a person inside inverted commas. Indirect or reported speech narrates what was said from the narrator's perspective without using exact quotes.
topicIntroduction.hi: प्रत्यक्ष कथन (Direct Speech) वक्ता के मूल शब्दों को उद्धरण चिह्नों में रखता है। अप्रत्यक्ष कथन (Reported Speech) उन शब्दों को अपनी भाषा में प्रस्तुत करता है।
topicIntroduction.te: డైరెక్ట్ స్పీచ్ లో వ్యక్తి మాట్లాడిన ఖచ్చితమైన మాటలు కొటేషన్లలో ఉంటాయి. ఇండైరెక్ట్ స్పీచ్ లో ఆ మాటల భావాన్ని మన మాటలలో చెబుతాము.

whyLearn.en: Essential for journalistic reporting, academic essay synthesis, professional business minutes, formal correspondence, and board examinations.
whyLearn.hi: समाचार लेखन, आधिकारिक पत्र व्यवहार, संवाद सारांश और बोर्ड परीक्षाओं के लिए अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण।
whyLearn.te: వార్తా రచన, వ్యాసాలు, అధికారిక ఉత్తర ప్రత్యుత్తరాలు మరియు పరీక్షల కోసం ఎంతో ముఖ్యం.

learningObjectives: Apply tense backshifting rules when the reporting verb is in the past tense
Accurately adjust first and second person personal/possessive pronouns to third person
Transform time, place, and proximity markers (e.g. today -> that day, tomorrow -> the next day)
Identify exceptions where universal scientific truths retain present tense

prerequisiteKnowledge.en: Classification of tenses: Simple Present, Present Continuous, Present Perfect, Simple Past, and Past Perfect.
prerequisiteKnowledge.hi: कालों का ज्ञान: सामान्य वर्तमान, अपूर्ण वर्तमान, पूर्ण वर्तमान, सामान्य भूतकाल।
prerequisiteKnowledge.te: టెన్సెస్ వర్గీకరణ మరియు వాటి సహాయక క్రియల పరిజ్ఞానం.

principlesAndRules.heading: Complete Tense Backshifting Matrix

rule.en:
Simple Present ("am/is/are/write") -> Simple Past ("was/were/wrote")
Present Continuous ("is writing") -> Past Continuous ("was writing")
Present Perfect ("has written") -> Past Perfect ("had written")
Simple Past ("wrote") -> Past Perfect ("had written")
Modals: can -> could, will -> would, may -> might, must -> had to
rule.hi: Simple Present -> Simple Past; Present Continuous -> Past Continuous; Present Perfect -> Past Perfect; Simple Past -> Past Perfect; can -> could; will -> would.
rule.te: Simple Present -> Simple Past; Present Continuous -> Past Continuous; Present Perfect -> Past Perfect; Simple Past -> Past Perfect; can -> could; will -> would.

principlesAndRules.formulaOrStructure: Subject + Reporting Verb + that + Transformed Pronoun + Backshifted Verb

diagramsAndTables.title: Time & Place Adverbial Conversion Table

description.en: Standard shifts of proximity expressions into distal reported markers.
description.hi: समय और स्थान सूचक शब्दों के परिवर्तन की तालिका।
description.te: సమయ మరియు స్థాన సూచికల మార్పు పట్టిక.

diagramsAndTables.asciiDiagramOrTable:
+--------------------+-------------------------------------+
| Direct Speech      | Reported (Indirect) Speech          |
+--------------------+-------------------------------------+
| now                | then                                |
| today              | that day                            |
| tonight            | that night                           |
| yesterday          | the previous day / the day before   |
| tomorrow           | the next day / the following day    |
| last week          | the previous week                   |
| here               | there                               |
| this / these       | that / those                        |
+--------------------+-------------------------------------+

realWorldApplications.en: Courtroom Legal Transcripts: Testimonies given by witnesses must be recorded in indirect speech with precise tense fidelity to preserve evidentiary chronology.
realWorldApplications.hi: अदालती कार्यवाही: गवाहों के बयानों को काल की सटीकता के साथ अप्रत्यक्ष कथन में दर्ज किया जाता है।
realWorldApplications.te: న్యాయస్థాన ప్రక్రియలు: సాక్షుల వాంగ్మూలాలను ఖచ్చితమైన కాల క్రమంలో పరోక్ష కథనంలో నమోదు చేస్తారు.

importantPoints.en: Universal Scientific Truths & Habits: Do NOT change tense if statement describes permanent natural laws (e.g. "He said that water boils at 100°C").
importantPoints.hi: सार्वभौमिक सत्य और वैज्ञानिक नियमों का काल कभी नहीं बदलता (जैसे जल 100°C पर उबलता है)।
importantPoints.te: సార్వత్రిక సత్యాలు మరియు శాస్త్రీయ నియమాల కాలం మారదు (ఉదా: నీరు 100°C వద్ద మరుగుతుంది).

revisionNotes.en: Rule Checklist: (1) Check reporting verb tense. (2) Replace inverted commas with "that". (3) Shift pronouns. (4) Backshift verbs (Present->Past, Past->Past Perfect). (5) Adjust time expressions.
revisionNotes.hi: जाँच सूची: रिपोर्टिंग वर्ब -> उद्धरण हटाएं -> सर्वनाम बदलें -> काल पीछे खिसकाएं -> समय सूचक बदलें।
revisionNotes.te: ముఖ్య నియమాలు: రిపోర్టింగ్ వెర్బ్ -> కొటేషన్లు తొలగించి that చేర్చడం -> సర్వనామాల మార్పు -> టెన్స్ మార్పు -> సమయ సూచికల మార్పు.

topicSummary.en: Reported speech allows seamless narration of dialogue. Mastery hinges upon synchronizing pronoun perspective, chronological tense backshifting, and situational adverbial conversions.
topicSummary.hi: परोक्ष कथन संवादों को सुचारू रूप से प्रस्तुत करता है। सर्वनाम और काल का सही संतुलन ही इसकी कुंजी है।
topicSummary.te: ఇండైరెక్ట్ స్పీచ్ ఇతరుల సంభాషణలను ప్రభావవంతంగా చెప్పడానికి తోడ్పడుతుంది.

question.en: What does "She said, 'I am writing an essay now'" become in indirect speech?
question.hi: "She said, 'I am writing an essay now'" अप्रत्यक्ष कथन में क्या बनेगा?
question.te: "She said, 'I am writing an essay now'" ఇండైరెక్ట్ స్పీచ్ లో ఎలా మారుతుంది?

answer.en: She said that she was writing an essay then.
answer.hi: She said that she was writing an essay then.
answer.te: She said that she was writing an essay then.

quickTip.te: "am writing" కాస్త "was writing" గాను, "now" కాస్త "then" గాను మారుతుంది.

instruction.en: Convert the following dialogue into indirect speech:
instruction.hi: निम्नलिखित वाक्य को अप्रत्यक्ष कथन में बदलें:
instruction.te: కింది వాక్యాన్ని ఇండైరెక్ట్ స్పీచ్ లోకి మార్చండి:

exerciseProblem.en: The librarian said to the students, "You must return all borrowed encyclopedias by tomorrow."
exerciseProblem.hi: The librarian said to the students, "You must return all borrowed encyclopedias by tomorrow."
exerciseProblem.te: The librarian said to the students, "You must return all borrowed encyclopedias by tomorrow."

solutionHint.en: "must" backshifts to "had to", "you" becomes "they", and "tomorrow" becomes "the next day".
solutionHint.hi: "must" बदलकर "had to" बनेगा और "tomorrow" -> "the next day"।
solutionHint.te: "must" కాస్త "had to" గాను, "tomorrow" కాస్త "the next day" గాను మారుతుంది.

lessons.title: Lens Formula, Magnification & New Cartesian Sign Convention

topicIntroduction.en: A lens is a transparent optical medium bounded by two spherical surfaces or one spherical and one planar surface. Lenses form images by refraction governed by Snell's law and curvature geometry.
topicIntroduction.hi: लेंस दो गोलीय पृष्ठों या एक गोलीय व एक समतल पृष्ठ से घिरा पारदर्शी माध्यम है जो अपवर्तन द्वारा प्रतिबिंब बनाता है।
topicIntroduction.te: కటకం అనేది రెండు గోళాకార తలాలు లేదా ఒక గోళాకార మరియు ఒక సమతలంతో కూడిన పారదర్శక యానకం.

whyLearn.en: Essential for designing corrective optical spectacles for myopia and hypermetropia, microscopes, telescopes, smartphone cameras, and ophthalmic laser surgery.
whyLearn.hi: नेत्र दोषों (निकट व दूर दृष्टि दोष) के निवारण हेतु चश्मों, सूक्ष्मदर्शी और कैमरों के निर्माण के लिए आवश्यक।
whyLearn.te: కంటి దోషాల నివారణ కళ్లద్దాలు, మైక్రోస్కోప్‌లు, టెలిస్కోప్‌లు మరియు కెమెరాల రూపకల్పనకు ఇది అత్యంత ముఖ్యం.

learningObjectives: Define optical center (O), principal axis, principal foci (F1, F2), and focal length (f)
Apply the New Cartesian Sign Convention rigorously: distances measured against incident light are negative
Solve numerical problems using the Lens Formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u
Calculate linear magnification (m = v/u = h_i / h_o) and deduce image nature and orientation

prerequisiteKnowledge.en: Laws of refraction: Incident ray, refracted ray, and normal lie in the same plane; Snell's Law (sin i / sin r = constant).
prerequisiteKnowledge.hi: अपवर्तन के नियम: स्नेल का नियम (sin i / sin r = स्थिरांक)।
prerequisiteKnowledge.te: వక్రీభవన నియమాలు: స్నెల్ నియమం (sin i / sin r = స్థిరాంకం).

explanation.en: In ray optics with spherical lenses, all distances are measured along the principal axis from the Optical Center (O) as origin. According to the New Cartesian Sign Convention: (1) Object is always placed to the left of the lens; (2) Distances measured in the direction of incident light (to the right of O) are POSITIVE (+); (3) Distances measured opposite to the direction of incident light (to the left of O) are NEGATIVE (-); (4) Heights measured upward perpendicular to principal axis are positive (+); heights downward are negative (-). A convex lens converges parallel incident light to a real focus on the right side, so its focal length is ALWAYS POSITIVE (f > 0). A concave lens diverges light from a virtual focus on the left, so its focal length is ALWAYS NEGATIVE (f < 0).
explanation.hi: लेंस में सभी दूरियां प्रकाशिक केंद्र (O) से मापी जाती हैं। आपतित प्रकाश की दिशा (दाईं ओर) में दूरियां धनात्मक (+) तथा विपरीत (बाईं ओर) ऋणात्मक (-) होती हैं। उत्तल लेंस की फोकस दूरी सदैव धनात्मक (f > 0) और अवतल लेंस की सदैव ऋणात्मक (f < 0) होती है।
explanation.te: కటకంలో అన్ని దూరాలను కటక కేంద్రం (O) నుండి కొలుస్తారు. కాంతి కిరణాల దిశలో దూరాలు ధనాత్మకం (+), వ్యతిరేక దిశలో రుణాత్మకం (-). కుంభాకార కటక నాభ్యాంతరం ఎల్లప్పుడూ ధనాత్మకం (f > 0), పుటాకార కటక నాభ్యాంతరం ఎల్లప్పుడూ రుణాత్మకం (f < 0).

definition.en: The mathematical relation connecting focal length (f), object distance (u), and image distance (v): 1/f = 1/v - 1/u.
definition.hi: फोकस दूरी (f), वस्तु दूरी (u) और प्रतिबिंब दूरी (v) के बीच संबंध: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u।
definition.te: నాభ్యాంతరం (f), వస్తు దూరం (u), మరియు ప్రతిబింబ దూరం (v) ల మధ్య సంబంధం: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u.

definition.en: The ratio of the height of the image (h_i) to the height of the object (h_o): m = h_i / h_o = v / u.
definition.hi: प्रतिबिंब की ऊंचाई और वस्तु की ऊंचाई का अनुपात: m = h_i / h_o = v / u।
definition.te: ప్రతిబింబ ఎత్తు మరియు వస్తువు ఎత్తుల నిష్పత్తి: m = h_i / h_o = v / u.

principlesAndRules.heading: Lens Formula vs Mirror Formula Sign Discipline

rule.en:
Lens Formula has a MINUS sign: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u (with magnification m = +v/u).
Mirror Formula has a PLUS sign: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u (with magnification m = -v/u). Do not confuse them!
rule.hi: लेंस सूत्र में माइनस (-) होता है: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u (आवर्धन m = +v/u)। दर्पण सूत्र में प्लस (+) होता है।
rule.te: కటక సూత్రంలో మైనస్ (-) ఉంటుంది: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u (ఆవర్ధనం m = +v/u). దర్పణ సూత్రంలో ప్లస్ (+) ఉంటుంది.

problem.en: A convex lens of focal length 15 cm forms a real image at a distance of 30 cm from the lens. Find the position of the object and the magnification produced.
problem.hi: 15 cm फोकस दूरी वाला उत्तल लेंस 30 cm की दूरी पर वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब बनाता है। वस्तु की स्थिति और आवर्धन ज्ञात करें।
problem.te: 15 cm నాభ్యాంతరం గల కుంభాకార కటకం 30 cm దూరంలో నిజ ప్రతిబింబం ఏర్పరుస్తుంది. వస్తువు దూరం మరియు ఆవర్ధనం కనుగొనండి.

stepByStep.en: Step 1 (Identify given with signs): f = +15 cm (convex lens), v = +30 cm (real image formed on right side). Find u.
stepByStep.hi: चरण 1: उत्तल लेंस के लिए f = +15 cm, वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब हेतु v = +30 cm।
stepByStep.te: దశ 1: f = +15 cm, v = +30 cm (నిజ ప్రతిబింబం కుడివైపు ఏర్పడుతుంది).

stepByStep.en: Step 2 (Apply lens formula): 1/f = 1/v - 1/u  =>  1/15 = 1/30 - 1/u.

stepByStep.hi: चरण 3: 1/u = -1/30  =>  u = -30 cm (वस्तु लेंस के 30 cm बाईं ओर है)।
stepByStep.te: దశ 3: 1/u = -1/30  =>  u = -30 cm (వస్తువు కటకానికి ఎడమవైపు 30 సెం.మీ దూరంలో ఉంది).

stepByStep.en: Step 4 (Calculate magnification): m = v / u = (+30) / (-30) = -1. Negative sign confirms image is real and inverted, of identical size.
stepByStep.hi: चरण 4: m = v / u = 30 / (-30) = -1। ऋणात्मक चिन्ह दर्शाता है कि प्रतिबिंब वास्तविक, उल्टा और बराबर आकार का है।
stepByStep.te: దశ 4: m = v / u = 30 / (-30) = -1. మైనస్ గుర్తు ప్రతిబింబం నిజమైనది, తలక్రిందులైనది మరియు సమాన పరిమాణం కలదని తెలుపుతుంది.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: u = -30 cm, m = -1 (Real, inverted, same size as object at 2F1)

keyInsight.en: When object is located at 2F (30 cm = 2 x 15 cm), image is formed at 2F on the other side with m = -1.
keyInsight.hi: जब वस्तु 2F पर होती है, तो प्रतिबिंब दूसरी तरफ 2F पर समान आकार का (m = -1) बनता है।
keyInsight.te: వస్తువు 2F వద్ద ఉన్నప్పుడు ప్రతిబింబం కూడా రెండవ వైపు 2F వద్ద సమాన పరిమాణంతో ఏర్పడుతుంది.

diagramsAndTables.title: Cartesian Sign Convention Diagram for Spherical Lenses

description.en: Coordinate axes overlaid on a spherical lens with optical center O at origin (0,0).
description.hi: गोलीय लेंस के लिए कार्तीय चिन्ह परिपाटी आरेख।

diagramsAndTables.asciiDiagramOrTable:
+y (Upward height: Positive)
                             |
    Incident Light ------>   |
  Distances against light:   |   Distances along light:
